issues.body: The old text ('the consequences of triple terms for canonicalization are unsettled upstream (see w3c/rdf-star-wg#114)') was a hedged claim carrying a re-check pointer. The new text — 'no W3C RDF-1.2 dataset-canonicalization specification exists' — is a stronger, absolute, undated claim about the outside world, and the diff simultaneously deletes the only reference a reader or a future agent could follow to confirm it. Two consequences: (a) if the W3C RDF 1.2 WG has (or later has) an editor's draft / Working Draft / chartered deliverable on canonicalization, 'no specification exists' reads as false while 'unsettled upstream' would still have been true, and nothing in the doc tells the reader where to look; (b) the citation was not removed for gate reasons — scripts/banned-terminology.json:200 explicitly allow-lists 'rdf-star-wg' as a legitimate proper-noun/URL citation, and skills/terminology/SKILL.md:106 names it a real citable body, warning that 'silent flattening of a precise prior-art reference is as much a documentation defect' as the reverse. The same wording lands in Cargo.toml, README.md, lib.rs and SKILL.md, so the observation applies to all five surfaces.
issues.fix_hint: Either keep the tracking link alongside the new phrasing (e.g. '... no W3C RDF-1.2 dataset-canonicalization specification exists; the underlying question is tracked at w3c/rdf-star-wg#114'), or make the claim checkable and bounded: '... no W3C RDF-1.2 dataset-canonicalization Recommendation or Working Draft as of 2026-08'. Restore the '[w3c/rdf-star-wg#114]: https://github.com/w3c/rdf-star-wg/issues/114' reference definition in crates/sparq-canon/src/rdf12.rs if the link is reinstated.
issues.title: Cited hedge replaced by an undated, uncited absolute claim about external W3C state

issues.body: After this change the shipped surfaces say 'no W3C RDF-1.2 dataset-canonicalization specification exists', while research/rdf-canon-rdf12-triple-terms-upstream.md (lines 16, 27, 42, 188) and bead sq-hslb still frame the same fact as 'currently undefined / unsettled upstream (w3c/rdf-star-wg#114)'. That is defensible — research/ records are dated historical artefacts and are deliberately not kept in lockstep — but a reader moving from the README to the design record now meets two different characterisations of the same upstream state with no bridge between them.
issues.fix_hint: No change required if the divergence is intentional. If a single voice is wanted, reuse one phrasing in both places, or add one clause to the README/SKILL note pointing at research/rdf-canon-rdf12-triple-terms-upstream.md as the record of the upstream questions this profile raised.
issues.title: Shipped docs and the in-repo research record now describe upstream status differently

verdict.summary: Docs-only change across 5 surfaces (sparq-canon Cargo.toml feature comment, crate README, lib.rs crate doc, rdf12.rs module + fn docs, skills/rdf-canon/SKILL.md). It replaces the hedged, cited phrasing 'RDF-1.2 canonicalization is unsettled upstream (w3c/rdf-star-wg#114)' with the absolute 'no W3C RDF-1.2 dataset-canonicalization specification exists', and drops the link. Correctness checks performed: (1) no code, test, or feature-gating change — behaviour is untouched, so no test is required and no test is rendered vacuous; (2) the load-bearing honesty labels all survive verbatim on every surface — NOT W3C RDFC-1.0, OFF by default, byte-identical with the feature OFF, standard paths still fail closed with CanonError::TripleTerm, W3C suite still passes — so the maintainer constraint from sq-hslb ('CLEARLY LABEL as non-standard, OPT-IN') is preserved; (3) the rustdoc reference-link removal is complete and self-consistent: rdf12.rs deletes both the sole usage and the '[w3c/rdf-star-wg#114]: ...' definition, and grep over crates/, skills/, site/, docs/ finds no surviving usage, so there is no dangling intra-doc/markdown link that could red the rustdoc --all-features half of the clippy gate; the still-used [RDFC-1.0] definition is retained; (4) all five occurrences of the old phrasing in shipped docs are updated together — no shipped surface is left with the old wording (remaining 'unsettled' hits in the tree are unrelated: OWL2-QL CQ, MPC estate recon, sparql_entail, reason-ql cq); (5) no security surface, no ZK/MPC privacy or soundness claim, no hard-coded performance number, no terminology-gate regression (rdf-star-wg is an allowPattern, not a ban, scripts/banned-terminology.json:200 — so the link was not required to be removed for the gate).
